findings.problem: hq1_cent (lines 111-121) and hq2_cent (lines 122-132) are the same argument with indices 1 and 2 swapped. Both do the following. They show ⁅q,q'⁆ ∈ Q. They show ⁅d*q₀, q⁆ = ⁅q₀, q⁆ by rewriting with commutatorElement_mul_left_eq_conj_mul, using that d commutes with q and with ⁅q₀,q⁆, and then running group. They then transfer centrality from T to Q with the hypothesis for the whole element d*q₀ via simpa. This is real reasoning (the Q-component of a Z2 element has centralised commutators), and it is copied wholesale, so a fix to one copy has to be made in the other.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a private lemma before u_Z2_commutator_eq:

private lemma u_Z2_Q_part_cent {T D Q : Subgroup G} {d q₀ : G}
    (hQT : Q ≤ T) (hDQ : ∀ d ∈ D, ∀ q ∈ Q, d * q = q * d)
    (hd : d ∈ D) (hq₀ : q₀ ∈ Q)
    (hs : ∀ t ∈ T, IsCentralIn T ⁅d * q₀, t⁆) :
    ∀ q ∈ Q, IsCentralIn Q ⁅q₀, q⁆ := by
  intro q hq
  have hmem : ⁅q₀, q⁆ ∈ Q := u_commutator_mem_of_mem hq₀ hq
  have h_eq : ⁅d * q₀, q⁆ = ⁅q₀, q⁆ := by
    rw [commutatorElement_mul_left_eq_conj_mul,
      commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.mpr (hDQ d hd q hq), mul_one,
      hDQ d hd ⁅q₀, q⁆ hmem]
    group
  refine ⟨hmem, fun q' hq' => ?_⟩
  have hc := (hs q (hQT hq)).2 q' (hQT hq')
  simpa only [h_eq] using hc

The proof is the existing block with d₁, q₁ and hs₁c generalised to d, q₀ and hs. Then in u_Z2_commutator_eq (after the two obtain ... rfl lines) replace both blocks with:

  have hq1_cent := u_Z2_Q_part_cent hQT hDQ hd₁ hq₁ hs₁c
  have hq2_cent := u_Z2_Q_part_cent hQT hDQ hd₂ hq₂ hs₂c

After the rfl substitutions, hs₁c : ∀ t ∈ T, IsCentralIn T ⁅d₁ * q₁, t⁆ and hs₂c : ∀ t ∈ T, IsCentralIn T ⁅d₂ * q₂, t⁆ (this is the unfolded u_Z2 second component), so both calls match the lemma's hs hypothesis. The rest of the proof (hq12, rw [u_commutator_mul_eq ...], exact hD2 ...) is unchanged.
findings.benefit: This removes about 20 duplicated lines and gives the step a name and a statement. Readers can see once that the Q-component of a Z2 element has Q-central commutators. A change to the argument is made in one place instead of two copies that could drift apart. The main lemma then reads as: extract two Q-components, apply hQ, and apply u_commutator_mul_eq.
